name: MAX17043 LiPo fuel gauge
description: Maxim (Analog Devices) single-cell Li-ion/LiPo fuel gauge with ModelGauge: reports cell voltage (12-bit, 1.25 mV steps, ±12.5 mV) and state of charge (1/256 %) over I2C at 0x36, with a low-SOC alert output and no sense resistor. The chip is powered from the battery itself (2.5–4.5 V). Sold as: SparkFun LiPo Fuel Gauge - MAX17043 (PRT-20680, v1.2; two 1x3 headers SDA/SCL/QST and VCC/GND/ALT plus a 2-pin JST battery connector with + / − pads), I2C address 0x36.
eli5: Sits on your LiPo battery's wires and tells your board the battery voltage and how full it is, in percent.

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (2.2 kΩ pull-up to VCC on the board, I2C jumper)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (2.2 kΩ pull-up to VCC on the board, I2C jumper)

pins.name: QST
pins.description: Quick-start input (chip QSTRT): a rising edge restarts the SOC estimate. Pulled to GND by a 2.2 kΩ resistor on the board; leave unconnected for normal use.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply for the I2C and alert pull-up resistors only, up to 5.5 V; use the microcontroller's logic voltage (3.3 V). The MAX17043 itself runs from the battery on the JST/+ − pads.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground, common with the battery's negative and the microcontroller

pins.name: ALT
pins.description: Alert output (chip ALRT), open-drain, active low, pulled up to VCC on the board: goes low when SOC falls below the alert threshold (default 4 %). Optional.

supplierQuery: SparkFun LiPo Fuel Gauge MAX17043 breakout
buildNotes: The pins sit on two 1x3 headers on opposite edges (SDA, SCL, QST and VCC, GND, ALT), so the board is wired with jumper leads.

Plug a 1-cell LiPo/Li-ion battery into the 2-pin JST connector (or solder to the + / − pads) and run the same pads to your system's battery input. The MAX17043 is powered by the battery: without one (or below 2.5 V) it does not answer on I2C.
VCC only feeds the 2.2 kΩ I2C / alert pull-ups (v1.2 board): give it the microcontroller's logic voltage, 3.3 V on ESP32/Pico. Never connect the battery's + to VCC or a GPIO.
Registers are 16-bit words read MSB first: VCELL (0x02) >> 4 × 1.25 mV = volts; SOC (0x04) / 256 = percent. CONFIG (0x0C) default 0x971C.
If SDA and SCL are both held low for 2.5 s (e.g. the microcontroller is unpowered) the chip goes to sleep; any edge on SDA/SCL wakes it.
SOC is a first guess right after the battery is connected and gets more accurate over time; only quick-start while the cell is resting.

driver.code:
# MAX17043 1-cell LiPo / Li-ion fuel gauge (Maxim / Analog Devices MAX17043-MAX17044 datasheet),
# MicroPython driver. I2C address 0x36 (0x6C write / 0x6D read). Every register is a 16-bit word
# sent MSB first at an even byte address; reads and writes are only valid if all 16 bits are moved
# in one transaction.
#   VCELL 0x02: 12-bit result in bits 15..4 (bits 3..0 read 0), 1.25 mV per count
#   SOC   0x04: high byte = whole percent, low byte = 1/256 %
#   MODE  0x06: write 0x4000 = quick-start
#   VERSION 0x08, CONFIG 0x0C (default 0x971C: RCOMP 0x97, SLEEP bit 7, ALRT bit 5, ATHD bits 4..0)
#   COMMAND 0xFE: write 0x5400 = power-on reset
# The chip is powered from the battery (VDD 2.5-4.5 V), so it does not answer until a cell is connected.

_REG_VCELL = 0x02
_REG_SOC = 0x04
_REG_MODE = 0x06
_REG_VERSION = 0x08
_REG_CONFIG = 0x0C
_REG_CMD = 0xFE


class MAX17043:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x36):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        try:
            self.version = self._read(_REG_VERSION)
        except OSError:
            raise OSError('MAX17043 not found at 0x%02X: is a battery connected?' % addr)

    def _read(self, reg):
        d = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, 2)
        return (d[0] << 8) | d[1]

    def _write(self, reg, value):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes([(value >> 8) & 0xFF, value & 0xFF]))

    def voltage(self):
        """Cell voltage in volts: VCELL >> 4 counts of 1.25 mV (updated every 500 ms)."""
        return (self._read(_REG_VCELL) >> 4) * 0.00125

    def soc(self):
        """State of charge in percent (high byte = %, low byte = 1/256 %). First valid 125 ms after POR."""
        return self._read(_REG_SOC) / 256

    def read(self):
        """Return (cell voltage in V, state of charge in %)."""
        return self.voltage(), self.soc()

    # --- alert --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def alert(self):
        """True while the CONFIG.ALRT flag is set (SOC fell below the alert threshold)."""
        return bool(self._read(_REG_CONFIG) & 0x0020)

    def clear_alert(self):
        """Clear CONFIG.ALRT so the ALRT pin releases (only software can clear it)."""
        self._write(_REG_CONFIG, self._read(_REG_CONFIG) & ~0x0020)

    def set_alert_threshold(self, percent):
        """Low-SOC alert threshold, 1-32 %: ATHD = 32 - percent (00000 = 32 %, 11111 = 1 %)."""
        percent = max(1, min(32, int(percent)))
        cfg = self._read(_REG_CONFIG)
        self._write(_REG_CONFIG, (cfg & ~0x001F) | ((32 - percent) & 0x1F))

    def set_rcomp(self, rcomp):
        """Battery compensation byte (CONFIG high byte, default 0x97)."""
        cfg = self._read(_REG_CONFIG)
        self._write(_REG_CONFIG, ((rcomp & 0xFF) << 8) | (cfg & 0x00FF))

    # --- control ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def quick_start(self):
        """Restart the SOC estimate from the present voltage (MODE = 0x4000). Only when the cell is
        relaxed (no heavy load or charging), otherwise the first guess is wrong."""
        self._write(_REG_MODE, 0x4000)

    def sleep(self, on=True):
        """CONFIG.SLEEP = 1 halts the gauge; writing it back to 0 wakes it (VCELL updates 500 ms later)."""
        cfg = self._read(_REG_CONFIG)
        self._write(_REG_CONFIG, (cfg | 0x0080) if on else (cfg & ~0x0080))

    def reset(self):
        """Power-on reset (COMMAND = 0x5400). The chip does not ACK this write."""
        try:
            self._write(_REG_CMD, 0x5400)
        except OSError:
            pass

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from max17043 import MAX17043

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
gauge = MAX17043(i2c)  # address 0x36; needs a battery plugged in
while True:
    v, soc = gauge.read()
    print('V=%.3fV SOC=%.1f%%' % (v, soc))
    time.sleep(1)
